Use Tier 2: change the ranking loss, focusing on model_design and training_evaluation. Replace the current mixture of uniform and detached hard-negative pairwise losses with sampled listwise cross-entropy over the positive item and the existing 64 uniformly sampled negatives. This is one controlled objective change; keep the history encoder, embeddings, scoring function, prefix sampling, optimizer, and training settings unchanged.

The pooling model achieved macro HR@10 of 0.4012, and adding sequential context reached 0.4100, both below the SASRec baseline of 0.505. These results justify investigating the objective, although they do not establish that it caused the performance gap. The current loss handles negative comparisons separately, whereas evaluation requires the positive to rank among a complete candidate list. Listwise cross-entropy makes all sampled candidates compete in one normalization and naturally concentrates gradients on high-scoring negatives. Continue masking sampled negatives that match the positive or observed prefix items before computing the loss.

Train one independent model per category and select exactly one checkpoint per category using validation HR@10, without averaging or auxiliary fitted scores. Preserve supplied splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four dataset routes, and artifacts beneath the trial directory. Keep validation fixed at 200 users per category with 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42, report macro HR@10, and retain identical learned scoring in validation and working/predict.py. Let the host perform held-out evaluation without accessing test files; treat improvement over the supplied results as a hypothesis to verify.
